source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: F I G U R E 2 Experimental Setup & Stimulation Scheme: (A) US & Electrophysiological Recording Setup: For electrical stimulation: Anesthetized male Sprague Dawley rats undergo sciatic nerve exposure surgery. The sciatic nerve is hooked to a bipolar silver-silver stimulating electrode. The electrode is driven via a stimulator and stimulus isolation unit to supply an electrical square wave of frequency 10 Hz, pulse duration 2 ms, and pulse amplitude 2.5/5/7.5 V. For US stimulation: A waveform generator supplies a continuous sine wave of frequency 200/500/700 kHz and amplitude $0 . 5 \mathsf { V } _ { \mathsf { p p } }$ to an Rf amplifier.

source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: Several stimulation parameters were randomized and applied. EMG recordings for each parameter combination lasted around 70 s. To study the effect of US stimulation on reflex arc, we first applied electrical stimulation for 20 s to activate nociceptive fibers and evoke muscle activity. This was followed by simultaneously applying US stimulation for 10 s. To study recovery, electrical stimulation of the nerve was maintained for 20 more seconds post-US stimulation.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Five male Sprague-Dawley rats weighing between 360-490 g were used in this study.
source_quotes.randomised: Several stimulation parameters were randomized and applied. The combination of parameters listed in Table 1 are 27 different combinations with 3 control stimulations (electrical stimulation only). Each of the 30 combinations are repeated 3 times in a random fashion, resulting in 90 recordings per experiment with 1 min of rest between stimulations.

flags.reason: Ultrasound characterization text states 'burst duration 12 ms' at 200/500/700 kHz, while the applied nerve-stimulation protocol states continuous-wave US applied for 10 s; unclear whether the 12 ms figure describes internal pulsing of the applied stimulus or is purely a calibration/characterization parameter, so pulse_duration_ms was left null rather than guessed.
Paper states waveform is a continuous sine wave but never gives an explicit duty-cycle percentage; left null rather than assuming 100%.
No inactive-transducer or sham-US condition was used; the only control condition was electrical stimulation alone (no US), classified here as 'none'.

Only water-tank (free-field) hydrophone-measured intensities are reported for the applied stimuli; no separate in-situ (derated/simulated/measured-in-tissue) values are given even though US was applied directly to an exposed nerve.

readout_other: EMG amplitude and area-under-the-curve of gastrocnemius muscle evoked potentials in response to electrical sciatic nerve stimulation; immunohistochemistry (anti-Neurofilament 200, anti-S100) of the sciatic nerve
direction_notes: US suppressed EMG amplitude and AUC of muscle-evoked potentials elicited by electrical sciatic-nerve stimulation; suppression was greater at the lower US frequency (200 kHz) and generally at lower acoustic intensities, persisted for 20 s post-stimulation, and recovered by ~30 min.
safety_notes: Temperature change upon US stimulation was less than 0.3°C; immunofluorescence showed no degradation of neurofilament or damage to axons/Schwann cells following ultrasound stimulation.

exposures.label: 200 kHz continuous-wave US to sciatic nerve

timing.protocol_description: Electrical stimulation was applied to the sciatic nerve for 20 s to evoke muscle activity, then continuous-wave US was applied simultaneously with electrical stimulation for 10 s, followed by 20 s of electrical stimulation alone to assess recovery. Each of 27 US/electrical parameter combinations plus 3 electrical-only controls was repeated three times in randomized order (90 recordings total per experiment), with 1 min rest between stimulations. During transducer characterization (not necessarily identical to the in-nerve exposure protocol), the transducer was described as operating with a 'burst duration 12 ms'.
